last_report.behaviour_change:
compare_parity_controls now judges the three decisive controls differently. It uses a new model-free statistic that analyze_modified_ramsey_record stores as acf["lag_covariance_sum"]: the autocovariance of the drift-corrected trace summed over lags 1..K, with K = ceil(expected dwell / dt). Lag 0 is excluded, so uncorrelated shots of any P(e) give about 0. Its 95% CI comes from a block bootstrap. Each control is reported as a ratio to the parity record (lag_cov_ratio), with its 5% and 95% bootstrap bounds.

(1) echo_null passes when the control HMM is unidentifiable through its i.i.d. gate, or when the lag ratio's 95% upper bound is < 0.25. It fails whenever the lag ratio's 5% lower bound is >= 0.25, because the telegraph clearly survived. The following no longer count as null evidence: the HMM's resolved-rate gate ((g01+g10)*dt > 1), an HMM optimizer failure, and an ACF fit failure. The resolved-rate gate is excluded because a partially refocused echo, fitted with the parity mapping, trips it.

(2) flip_final_pi2 needs three things: the ACF amplitude ratio > 0.25, an identifiable flip HMM, and an effective rate (g01+g10)/2 that agrees with the parity record's. The rates count as disagreeing only if they differ by more than 3 combined 1-sigma errors AND by more than a factor of 2, so ordinary drift between records is tolerated. The occupancy inversion is then tested only when |occ1_main - 0.5| > 0.15. For a balanced parity record the verdict is "inversion uninformative" (checked None), so a non-inverted balanced flip no longer passes.

(3) drive_off is now decisive with a 0.1 contamination budget. It passes if the lag ratio's 95% upper bound is < 0.1. It fails if the lag ratio itself is >= 0.1, with the note "inter-shot carryover / readout correlation contaminates the parity record". In between, the verdict is "inconclusive" (checked None): the record is too short to bound the ratio. Without the lag statistic, the ACF amplitude ratio decides: < 0.1 passes, otherwise fail.

Each entry carries "verdict", "lag_cov_ratio" and "lag_cov_ratio_upper95". all_expected requires a valid parity record, at least one decisive check, and no failed check.

last_report.notes:
Reviewer findings addressed:

(1) echo_null: the HMM-null branch now accepts only the i.i.d. gate (_HMM_IID_REASON_KEY = 'uncorrelated (i.i.d.)'), and a lag lower bound >= 0.25 vetoes a pass. I probed this on the parity record from seeds 72/73. All five ideal nulls trip the i.i.d. gate: P(e)=0.5 trips it together with the unresolved gate, and the others alongside too-few-switches or pinned-rate reasons. Every partial echo trips only 'unresolved'. With the fix, all three 0.29/0.71 seeds fail. The pre-review code passed two of them, reproducing the reviewer's result. The 0.32/0.68 partial echoes have a true lag ratio of ~0.2, below the documented 0.25 threshold, so they pass on the lag statistic when their upper bound is < 0.25. That is correct under the threshold's own definition. The veto uses the 5% lower bound rather than the point estimate, so a noisy lag statistic on a short record cannot overturn a genuine i.i.d. verdict.

(2) flip rate check: rate disagreement now needs both > 3 combined sigma and a ratio > FLIP_RATE_MAX_RATIO = 2.0. The reviewer's 230 vs 200 Hz drift case at 100k-shot errors now passes. The full-pipeline 3x (600 Hz) flip still fails.

(3) drive_off: I chose the documentation route for the threshold and also removed the extra strictness. The fail rule is now 'point ratio >= 0.1', as the finding asked. Passing needs the 95% upper bound < 0.1, and the gap between the two is 'inconclusive' (not decisive) instead of a fail. I did not raise the threshold. The 2026-08-04 parity arms later showed no significant parity contrast (r(1) excess t = 1.33), so a drive_off at 25-40% of that record's correlation does indicate contamination. Simulation result: with an OU readout drift (tau 122 ms) after the 200 ms rolling-mean drift removal, at dt 262 us and K = 10, lag_cov_ratio / ACF amplitude ratio is ~1.5-1.6 (drift sd 0.5/0.7/1.0 gave ACF ratios 0.096/0.19/0.39 and lag ratios 0.15/0.30/0.62). A 50 ms drift window cut the 0.7 case from 0.30 to 0.074.

The new constant is FLIP_RATE_MAX_RATIO, and _lag_cov_ratio also returns lower05; it stays internal and is not a new entry field. Verification all passed: compileall, ruff check --select F over qicklab runners tests devices, ruff format on both touched .py files, and pytest on tests/test_modified_ramsey_offline.py, tests/test_run_modified_ramsey_controls.py, tests/test_imports.py and tests/test_program_timing.py. diff_labels as described above.

findings.claim: In echo_null, a positive HMM 'resolved-rate' gate overrides model-free evidence that the telegraph survived. The echo HMM is fitted with the parity record's assumed mapping (0.1/0.9), so a partially refocused echo is mis-modelled, the HMM locks onto a fast rate and reports 'unresolved at this cadence', and the echo passes even when the lag statistic says it is not suppressed.
findings.evidence: I probed this on the implementer's own 20k-sample, 262 us, 200 Hz parity record (seed 72/73). I added a leaky echo carrying the same 200 Hz telegraph with mapping 0.29/0.71. Two of three seeds gave checked=True, with lag_cov_ratio 0.293 / 0.271 and upper95 0.333 / 0.312, both above the 0.25 threshold. The only HMM reason was '(gamma01 + gamma10) * dt = 1.12 > 1: switching unresolved...'. The 0.27/0.73 cases stayed identifiable and failed correctly. The old code had the same OR, so this is not a regression, and it sits near the threshold (true covariance ratio ~0.30). It still goes against the point of adding a model-free statistic. Suggested fix: when the lag statistic is available and its lower bound (or point estimate) exceeds 0.25, let it veto the HMM-null branch, or accept only the i.i.d. gate as HMM null evidence (the finding text says 'by the i.i.d. gate'). Add the leaky 0.29/0.71 case to the tests.

findings.claim: The flip rate-agreement test uses only the statistical Hessian errors (3 combined sigma). With a balanced parity record (the expected symmetric case) the flip can now only be 'uninformative' or 'failed', so ordinary drift of the parity rate between the parity and flip records fails the control and forces all_expected=False on good data.
findings.evidence: Calibration: 25 seed pairs at identical rates gave z-score std 0.94 and no failures, so the Hessian errors are well calibrated statistically. A drift does fail it, though. At N=100k (the shot count the docs recommend), the relative error is 2.3%. A flip whose true rate was 230 Hz against a 200 Hz main record failed (249 vs 214 Hz, combined sigma 7.3), and at 400k shots a ~5% drift would fail. Quasiparticle and parity rates commonly drift by more than that between records taken minutes apart. Add a systematic tolerance floor (e.g. relative, comparable to estimator_agreement_factor), or record a rate mismatch as a flag rather than a fail. If you keep it as is, document it as a known false-alarm mode.

findings.claim: The decisive drive_off threshold (95% upper bound < 0.1) is not validated against the project's own CSTQ03 numbers. Those numbers suggest the accepted relax configuration sits near a ratio of 0.25, so adding drive_off to the defaults, as the new docs recommend, would likely fail good runs.
findings.evidence: docs/devices/CSTQ03.md and docs/experiments/modified_ramsey.md, 2026-08-04: at 200 us relax the ACF amplitude was 0.000575 for drive_off against 0.002301 for parity, a ratio of 0.25. That residual is attributed to slow readout drift (tau ~122 ms), not to T1. The 250 us acceptance run gave r(1) of +0.003 for drive_off against +0.011 for parity (~0.27). The implementer also made the rule stricter than the finding: the finding asked for the ratio to be < 0.1, while the code requires the bootstrap upper bound to be < 0.1. The threshold comes from the finding's proposal, but the docs note at modified_ramsey.md:368-369 ('add it when the inter-shot reset has to be checked') should warn that slow-drift residuals may exceed 0.1. Otherwise justify the 0.1 threshold against the drift-corrected lag statistic.

findings.claim: _lag_cov_ratio requires only the 5th percentile of the parity bootstrap to be above 0. Up to 5% of the denominator replicates can therefore be zero or negative, or close to zero, which inflates or destabilises the ratio's 95th percentile. The error is conservative: it makes passes harder. It is negligible when the parity record is strongly significant, as in every test.
findings.evidence: ratio_boot = c_boot[:n] / m_boot[:n][::-1], with the gate at np.percentile(m_boot, 5) > 0.

findings.claim: The flip survival check still uses the ACF amplitude ratio, which the implementer's own notes call unreliable on weak records. The lag-covariance ratio could serve as the survival measure for consistency. _effective_rate for asymmetric fits ignores the g01/g10 covariance in the Hessian. Both are minor.
findings.evidence: survives = math.isfinite(ratio) and ratio > 0.25 (ACF amplitude); err = 0.5*hypot(e01, e10).

last_review.summary: F16 does what the finding asks, analysis only, and the tests pin it. On the HEAD code the balanced non-inverted flip and the failed-HMM echo both passed and drive_off was informational; all three now give the new verdicts. The bootstrap lag-covariance statistic is computed correctly: the AR(1) check holds, white noise covers 0, and the Hessian-error rate test is statistically calibrated (z std 0.94 over 25 seed pairs). The echo HMM-null branch matches the actual hmm.py reason strings. No unintended code changes. diff_labels shows only the concurrent yoko_writes leaves, and I confirmed the golden is unaffected, as expected since the frozen runner does not run the analysis. Not editing modified_ramsey_control.md is justified. Three physics should-fixes remain. (1) The echo's resolved-rate HMM gate can override model-free evidence of a surviving telegraph: 0.29/0.71 leaky echoes with lag upper95 0.31-0.33 still pass. (2) The flip rate check uses only statistical errors, so ordinary parity-rate drift between records fails good flips: a 15% drift fails at 100k shots. (3) The drive_off < 0.1 upper-bound threshold sits below the ~0.25 ratio the CSTQ03 2026-08-04 data shows for accepted relax settings. None is a regression or an unintended change, so I approve with these as follow-ups.
